Free will is a magical concept. I'm not speaking in metaphor either, it actually would require magic to be true.

Everything that we know shows us that the universe is ruled by the laws of physics, even if we do not 100% understand what those laws are.

Our brains are physical structures in this universe. Our minds or "consciousness" are emergent properties of our complex brains and can be altered by altering the chemical or physical make-up of the brain.

Yet those that believe in free will would have you believe that by virtue of being conscious we somehow are able to escape causality, that our minds escape the laws of physics to which our brain is bound. Yet, pump them full of a few strong alcoholic beverages and you can watch their mind deteriorate. If they take a piece of shrapnel to the right places in the brain, any number of deleterious effects on their mental capabilities can be observed. Watch them consume stimulants, depressants, seratonin reuptake inhibitors, and various other chemicals and with a high likelihood you can predict changes in their behavior.

Think about that for a moment. They claim free will, but their behavior can be predicted to a statistical degree of certainty. Add the right chemical here and there and you arguably have a loose ability to control them.

Sure, there are a huge number of variables that enter into the uncertainty of the equation, like prior experiences and memories, but those exhibit themselves as changes in the structure of the brain within the innumerable synaptic connections. Body chemistry plays some role, but chemicals are still physical things. Genetics plays a role, but DNA is still a chemical and, as we just went over, still a physical thing.

Put all of the variables together and you have more possible variances than all of the people that have ever lived, currently live, or ever will live, but all of those iterations of the human mind are still accountable to physical law.

So where is the "escape" button? Where is the thing that disconnects the mind from physics and causality? Where is the magic that grants free will? There does not seem to be any evidence for it.

TL;DR - If chemistry and physics control the brain, and the brain controls the mind, there is no free will.

If you could sense all the motives and choose free, you could make a free decision. But that´s not possible!
